thread.title: National Park College enrollment tops 5,300 as concurrent ranks surge
thread.title_full: National Park College enrollment tops 5,300 as concurrent ranks surge

author: @TheSenRec
title: National Park College enrollment tops 5,300 as concurrent ranks surge
text:
National Park College has served more than 5,300 students this fall, with a sharp increase in concurrent enrollment helping offset a decline in traditional credit enrollment, according to a college news release.
Combined credit and noncredit enrollment reached more than 5,339 students for fall 2026, up from about 4,845 a year ago, the release said.
The college reported 2,630 credit and concurrent students, a 7% increase from last fall and the highest combined enrollment in seven years. Those students generated 25,864 credit hours, up 1.5%.
Concurrent enrollment, which allows high school students to earn college credit, climbed to 989 students, a 42% increase from last fall. Concurrent students generated 5,846 credit hours, up 41%.
Traditional credit enrollment declined, however. Vice President for Student Affairs and Enrollment Management Darla Thurber reported 1,641 credit students at the 11th-day census, down from 1,756 last fall. Credit hours among those students fell from 21,314 to 20,018.
"We are excited to see so many students choosing National Park College as part of their educational journey," Thurber said in the release. "These enrollment numbers demonstrate the value students and families place on affordable, high-quality education and workforce training opportunities close to home."
NPC enrolled 600 first-time students this fall, its highest number since 2012 and a 2% increase from last year.
Transfer enrollment also increased. The college reported 102 transfer students, up 12%, while credit hours generated by transfer students rose 25%.
NPC also reported growth in its Workforce and Community Education Division. Noncredit programs have served 2,709 students since July 1, a 13% increase from the same period last year. Child Care Aware child care worker training grew from 365 students to 681, an 87% increase.
Adult Education programs have served 725 students, up 25% from the same period last year.
The college said workforce training and its Makerspace also saw increased participation with community partners, while apprenticeship enrollment remained steady.
Enrollment declined at the NPC Career Academy after new requirements took effect. Students in those programs must now qualify for concurrent credit by meeting minimum ACT or Accuplacer scores, according to the release.
Continuing education programs and summer camps also recorded slight enrollment declines.
